titulo: Unreal Past, Modal Perfect and Third Conditional
descripcion: At B2 the three regret structures — wish, modal perfect, third conditional — are learned individually and start to be combined in short exchanges. The seamless blending expected at C1 isn't the target yet; using each correctly, and occasionally together, is enough.

filas: regret about now or the past
if + past perfect, would have + participle

ejemplos.texto: I wish I'd known about it sooner.
We should have checked before leaving.
If we'd checked, we wouldn't have missed the train.

notas: Wish takes the past perfect when the regret is about the past: I wish I'd known, not I wish I knew, for a past event.
Should have is about a missed obligation; could have is about a missed possibility — they aren't interchangeable.
The if-clause of the third conditional never contains would.

es.en: Spanish expresses the same with ojalá + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo and with si + pluscuamperfecto + conditional perfect, and it also has the modal perfect (debería haberlo dicho, podría haberlo evitado). The logic is parallel; the difference is the form, since Spanish puts the modal in the conditional and English uses should / could have + participle.
es.es: El español expresa lo mismo con «ojalá» + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo y con «si» + pluscuamperfecto + condicional compuesto, y también tiene el modal perfecto («debería haberlo dicho», «podría haberlo evitado»). La lógica es paralela; cambia la forma, porque el español pone el modal en condicional y el inglés usa «should/could have» + participio.

de.en: German has close equivalents for all three pieces: ich wünschte, ich hätte… (I wish I had), hätte… sollen / können (should / could have) and hätte… in conditionals. The recurring error comes from colloquial würde: I wish I would have known, if I would have known.
de.de: Für alle drei Bausteine gibt es im Deutschen nahe Entsprechungen: «ich wünschte, ich hätte…» («I wish I had»), «hätte… sollen/können» («should/could have») und «hätte…» in Konditionalsätzen. Die wiederkehrenden Fehler kommen aus umgangssprachlichem «würde»: «I wish I would have known», «if I would have known».

it.en: Italian has a separate modal perfect (avrei dovuto, avrei potuto), so all three pieces exist. Translated literally, however, avrei dovuto dirtelo becomes I would have had to tell you instead of I should have told you.
it.it: L'italiano possiede un modal perfect separato («avrei dovuto», «avrei potuto»), quindi tutti e tre gli elementi esistono. Tradotto letteralmente, però, «avrei dovuto dirtelo» diventa «I would have had to tell you» invece di «I should have told you».

fr.en: French has a separate modal perfect (j'aurais dû, j'aurais pu) and si seulement j'avais su for regret, so all three pieces exist. Translated literally, j'aurais dû te le dire becomes I would have had to tell you instead of I should have told you.
fr.fr: Le français possède un modal perfect distinct («j'aurais dû», «j'aurais pu») et «si seulement j'avais su» pour le regret ; les trois éléments existent donc. Traduit littéralement, «j'aurais dû te le dire» devient «I would have had to tell you» au lieu de «I should have told you».

pt.en: Portuguese has the modal perfect in almost the same order as English (devia ter dito – should have said; podia ter evitado – could have avoided). Together with quem me dera ter sabido (I wish I had known), all three pieces transfer well.
pt.pt: O português tem o modal perfect quase na mesma ordem do inglês («devia ter dito» – «should have said»; «podia ter evitado» – «could have avoided»). Com «quem me dera ter sabido» («I wish I had known»), os três elementos se transferem bem.

errores: Using would in the if-clause of the third conditional.
Confusing should have and could have.
Using the past simple after wish for a past regret instead of the past perfect.

es: *tendría que haber ido* rendered as *I would have to have gone* instead of *I should have gone*.
de: *wenn … nur* rendered with *when*: *When I had only known* instead of *If only I had known*.
it: *sarei dovuto venire* rendered as *I would have had to come*, which changes the meaning, instead of *I should have come*.
fr: *j'aurais dû venir* rendered as *I would have had to come*, which changes the meaning, instead of *I should have come*.
pt: *devia ter vindo* rendered as *I had to come*, which states a fact, instead of *I should have come*.

traducciones.de: Wenn wir… hätten, hätten wir nicht…
traducciones.fr: Si nous avions…, nous n’aurions pas…

redemittel.funcion: regret about something that was done

redemittel.expresion: There was nothing we could have done.

traducciones.es: No había nada que pudiéramos haber hecho.
traducciones.pt: Não havia nada que pudéssemos ter feito.

redemittel.funcion: turns the regret into a plan

traducciones.fr: En fait, je ne le regrette pas.
traducciones.it: In realtà non me ne pento.

redemittel.funcion: hands the counterfactual to the other person

traducciones.pt: E tu, o que terias feito?

mision.consigna: Someone you met abroad is still annoyed about a misunderstanding between you. Write them a message looking back on it.
requisitos: one *I wish I'd…*, one *It's a shame that…*
one modal perfect and one third conditional
a different situation from the last time you wrote about regret
use *a misunderstanding*, *to fit in* and *a sense of belonging*

microtareas.texto: Three *I wish I'd…* sentences about living abroad.
Record 90 seconds: a *stereotype* you believed and shouldn't have.

autochequeo: Is the past perfect used after wish for a past regret?
Are should have and could have used correctly, not interchangeably?
Is the if-clause free of would?
Are at least two of the three structures used in the same passage?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on wish, modal perfect and the third conditional. Check for would inside the if-clause and the choice between should and could have. Do not rewrite the text.
